construction_markdown:
Let `p(T)=T^16+T^5+T^3+T+1`. Rabin's criterion certifies that `p` is irreducible over `F_2`: `T^(2^16)≡T mod p` and `gcd(p,T^(2^8)+T)=1`. Put `E=F_2[T]/(p)` and `theta=T mod p`.

Let `A=span_F2{1,theta,…,theta^14}`, ordered by its 15 coefficient bits, so `|A|=32768`. Write every `z∈E` uniquely as `z=sum_{i=0}^{15} z_i theta^i`. Define the binary inner block

`Phi(z)_y = z_0 + sum_{i=1}^{15} z_i y_i`, for `y∈F_2^15`,

with `y` in lexicographic order. This is a binary-linear bijection from `E` to `RM(1,15)`.

For `P(X)=sum_{j=0}^{64}a_jX^j∈E[X]`, define

`c_P=(Phi(P(alpha))_y)_{(alpha,y)∈A×F_2^15}`,

again in lexicographic order, and set `C={c_P:deg P≤64}`.

For the balanced-code interpretation, let `B≤C` be the hyperplane where the coefficient of `1` in the polynomial-basis expansion of `a_0` is zero. Then `dim(B)=1039`, every nonzero word of `B` has weight in `[535822336,537919488]`, and `C=B direct-sum <1^N>`. Thus the full `C` is the deterministic one-sided target code. No sampling, puncturing, shortening, padding, or unspecified finite choice occurs.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: In the degree-64 RS–affine code, every nonconstant `P` satisfies `|wt(c_P)-2^29|≤2^20`: the fibers `P^{-1}(0)` and `P^{-1}(1)` each have size at most 64. The only unbalanced nonzero word is `P=1`. Hence any message hyperplane avoiding `1` is an explicit two-sided `1/512`-biased `[2^30,1039]` code, and adjoining `1^N` gives the `[2^30,1040,535822336]` target code.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Can one give a deterministic sparse subfamily of free-expander or wide-replacement paths, with at most `2^30/n_0` paths per base coordinate, whose signed average is bounded by `1/512` simultaneously for every nonzero message? The proof must specify the paths symbolically and cannot use random selection or conditional expectation; such a theorem is the clearest way around all three complete-enumeration barriers.

distance_audit: The campaign deficit `2^-10` corresponds to signed-bias threshold `tau=2^-9=1/512`, since `(1-tau)N/2=(1/2-2^-10)N`.
For nonconstant `P`, both `P` and `P-1` are nonzero polynomials of degree at most 64, so their fibers over zero contain at most 64 elements of `A`.
If `N_i=|{alpha∈A:P(alpha)=i}|`, the inner weight distribution gives `wt(c_P)=2^14(32768-N_0+N_1)`. Hence `|wt(c_P)-2^29|≤64*2^14=2^20`.
A nonzero constant polynomial belonging to `B` cannot equal `1`; its inner affine function has a nonzero linear part and therefore total weight exactly `2^29`.
Adding the all-one direction complements words of `B`, so every nonzero word of `C` has weight at least `2^29-2^20=535822336`.
For exactness, a degree-64 polynomial with 64 prescribed roots can be scaled to avoid the value `1` on every nonroot. Its word has weight exactly `(32768-64)*16384=535822336`.
Because `C` is binary linear, this all-codeword weight audit proves the pairwise minimum distance.
explicitness_audit: The field is the displayed quotient by an explicit irreducible polynomial. The Rabin computation was independently recomputed; with bit `i` denoting `T^i`, the Euclidean remainder chain begins `0x1002b,0x50f2` and continues `0x1311,0x0fa7,0x03f8,0x0047,0x0015,0x0006,0x0001`.
The evaluation set is the displayed 15-dimensional coefficient hyperplane, not an existential subset.
Field elements, evaluation points, messages, outer blocks, and inner coordinates all use fixed polynomial-basis lexicographic order.
The inner map is given coordinate-by-coordinate and is binary-linear and injective.
The message space has exactly 65 coefficients over the explicitly represented 16-dimensional binary field.
The equality witness uses the first 64 evaluation points and the lexicographically first admissible nonzero scale. At most 32704 of the 65535 scales are forbidden.
There are no hidden floors, inherited parameters, random choices, padding coordinates, punctures, or numerical searches in the submitted construction.

All 23 durable submissions and all 23 message-board files present at the final audit were individually read; the shared lemma-book and roadmap directories were empty. The read-only workspace prevented persistence and publication-build commands, so this remains a leaderboard candidate rather than a records update.

parameter_ledger.derivation: One binary equation on 65 field coefficients

proof_markdown:
### 1. Normalization

For a binary word `c` of length `N`, its signed bias is `1-2 wt(c)/N`. Thus absolute bias at most `tau=1/512` places its weight in

`[(1-tau)N/2,(1+tau)N/2]=[2^29-2^20,2^29+2^20]`.

The lower endpoint is exactly `D=535822336`.

### 2. Field, linearity, length, and dimension

The displayed Rabin certificate proves that `E` is `F_{2^16}`. The polynomial basis fixes every field operation and ordering. The subspace `A` has exactly `2^15` elements.

`Phi` is binary-linear. If its truth table is zero, evaluation at `y=0` gives `z_0=0`, and evaluation at the fifteen unit vectors then gives every `z_i=0`; hence `Phi` is injective. Its nonzero words have weight `2^14`, except `Phi(1)`, which is all-one and has weight `2^15`.

Evaluation of degree-at-most-64 polynomials on `A` is injective: a nonzero polynomial cannot have 32768 roots. Consequently `C` is binary linear, has length

`|A|*2^15=2^15*2^15=2^30`,

and dimension `65*16=1040`.

### 3. The balanced hyperplane

Let `B` be the message hyperplane `[a_0]_0=0`, where `[a_0]_0` is the coefficient of `1` in the polynomial basis. It has dimension 1039 and does not contain `P=1`.

For nonconstant `P`, set `N_i=|{alpha∈A:P(alpha)=i}|`. Both `P` and `P-1` are nonzero of degree at most 64, so `N_0,N_1≤64`. Zero inner symbols contribute weight zero, the symbol `1` contributes `2^15`, and every other symbol contributes `2^14`. Therefore

`wt(c_P)=2^15 N_1+2^14(32768-N_0-N_1)=2^14(32768-N_0+N_1)`.

It follows that `|wt(c_P)-2^29|≤2^20`. If a nonzero `P∈B` is constant, then its constant basis bit is zero, so it is neither `0` nor `1`; its inner word is balanced and `wt(c_P)=2^29`. Hence every nonzero word of `B` lies in `[D,N-D]`.

The polynomial `P=1` encodes as `1^N` and is outside `B`, while every polynomial decomposes uniquely as an element of `B` plus either `0` or `1`. Thus `C=B direct-sum <1^N>`. Complementing a word in `[D,N-D]` preserves that interval, and `1^N` itself has weight `N`. Therefore every nonzero word of `C` has weight at least `D`.

### 4. Exact minimum distance

Let `R` be the first 64 elements of `A` and `P_0(X)=product_{r∈R}(X-r)`. For each of the 32704 nonroots, at most one nonzero scalar `lambda` makes `lambda P_0(alpha)=1`. Hence at most 32704 of the 65535 nonzero scalars are forbidden. Choose the first admissible scalar in polynomial-basis order.

The resulting `P_*=lambda P_0` is zero at exactly 64 evaluation points and takes neither `0` nor `1` elsewhere. Its codeword therefore has weight

`32704*2^14=2^29-2^20=D`.

Together with the lower bound, this proves `d_min(C)=535822336`.

### 5. Finite literature comparison

The classical complete constructions specialize as follows: AGHP powering gives balanced dimension 975; the extended dual-BCH trace code gives 990; the exact extended norm–trace optimization gives 444. The balanced hyperplane above gives 1039, and its all-one augmentation gives 1040.

The near-optimal asymptotic papers do not improve this finite value. Ta-Shma's exact complete-output theorem has no contracting rank-at-least-1041 instance under the length budget. Cohen–Cohen requires at least `261540414231` rows. For the 2026 free-expander schedule, `kappa=1` makes Lemma 2.12's exponent nonpositive and its upper bound greater than one; `kappa≥2` forces at least `2^32` lift paths. Recent trace-AG theorems retain hidden constants or explicitly obtain no improvement, while the low-rate concatenation papers use random constituents and numerical constants that already force dimension below one here.

These conclusions rule out the published certificates and complete-output architectures, not arbitrary future binary codes.
